newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab African Int'l Bank bond issue to close soon.
newsitem.headline: Arab African Int'l Bank bond issue to close soon.

text.p: A 300 million pound ($88 million) bond offer by the Arab African International Bank is almost fully subscribed and will close within a week, a senior bank official said on Sunday.

The bank had offered investors five-year floating-rate notes for at least 10 days from March 5 and Hassan Abdalla, head of the investment and treasury department, told Reuters it was giving foreign financial institutions time to get in the issue.
"It's almost fully subscribed, we've had very good demand and within the week it will be a done deal," Abdalla said.
"Foreign entities have expressed interest and we're keen to have international subscribers so we decided to give them until the end of the week," he added.

The notes will pay interest every three months, at 0.25 percentage points above the average yield on 91-day treasury bills over the three-month period, the bank said. The average yield on 91-day bills is now a fraction below 10 percent.
If the treasury does not issue 91-day bills, the interest will be 2.75 percentage points below the Central Bank discount rate, which now stands at 13 percent.
The notes will be in units of 1,000 pounds and the bank will issue them in lots of one, five, 10, 25, 50 and 100 notes, it said. The fee for issuing them will be two pounds per note.
Abdalla said that foreign investors were also trying to persuade the bank to issue U.S. dollar denominated bonds, an issue he said was still under consideration.
The bank said it made net profits of $1.88 million in the first nine months of calendar 1996, compared with $12.1 million in all of 1995 and $10.2 million in 1994.
But it forecast that net profits would rise to $15.576 million in 1997 and $18.789 million in 1998. They would keep rising through the next years to reach $33.582 million in 2002.
On September 30, 1996, it had total assets of $812.39 million, against $822.00 million at the end of 1995.
Shareholders' funds were worth $141.48 million at the end of the nine-month period, against $139.6 million at the end of 1995, it said. The bank has paid-in capital of $100 million.
The Central Bank of Egypt and the Kuwaiti Finance Ministry own 49.37 percent each and other shareholders the balance of 1.26 percent.
